compound.name: β-thujone
compound.one_liner: The less toxic thujone diastereomer (4-36 % of sage oil); counted with α-thujone in EMA limits.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Salvia officinalis L., folium and Salvia officinalis L., aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/150801/2015 (20 Sep 2016). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-salvia-officinalis-l-folium-and-salvia-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: BETA-THUJONE Leaf Essent. Oil 174000-356000 ppm; Leaf 200-9968 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil

pharmacology.mechanism: Same site as α-thujone with lower toxicity [39].

evidence.claim: β-Thujone is less toxic than α-thujone.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: see α-thujone (EMA thujone limits apply to total thujone)
safety_flags.source_citation: EMA/HMPC public statement on thujone, EMA/HMPC/732886/2010 Rev.1 (2012)

compound.teaching_note: Two thujones differ only in one stereocentre, yet differ in toxicity [39]: stereochemistry is pharmacology.
gaps: Whether EMA limits are for α+β combined is stated from the statement title ('thujone'); confirm wording.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
